topic.label: Film and Media Studies
topic.desc: Film and Media Studies: the history, theory, analysis and production of cinema, television and digital media.

concepts: How mise-en-scene, cinematography, editing and sound create meaning in a film.
The development of cinema from early film through national cinemas, studio systems, new waves and global art cinema.
Theories of realism, apparatus, spectatorship, semiotics, psychoanalysis, feminist and postcolonial critique of screen media.
Broadcast, cable and streaming television: seriality, scheduling, platforms and audiences.
Online video, social platforms, games and algorithmic culture as media forms.
Financing, production, distribution and regulation of media, plus hands-on filmmaking practice.
skills: Breaks a sequence into shots with scale, angle, movement and duration and checks the shot list against the timecodes.
Interprets how formal choices in a scene create meaning and checks every claim is tied to a specific visible or audible detail.
Maps plot, story time and point of view in a film and checks the map against scene order.
Profiles a movement such as Italian neorealism or the French New Wave with its context, style and key works and checks dates and attributions.
Traces a genre's conventions over time across representative films and checks each example's date and credits.
Identifies recurring style and themes across a director's films and checks each claim against named works.
Applies a theoretical framework such as the male gaze or Bazinian realism to a film and checks the application against the theorist's text.
Identifies signs, codes and connotations in an image or advertisement and checks each reading against visible evidence.
Searches peer-reviewed film and media scholarship through Wiley Scholar Gateway and checks each citation resolves to the stated work.
Analyses season and episode arcs in a series and checks arcs against an episode guide.
Explains how a streaming platform commissions, releases and recommends content and checks claims against company reporting.
Analyses how audiences interpret a programme from reviews and fan discourse and checks the sample is described.
Codes a sample of online videos or posts with a stated codebook and checks intercoder reliability.
Explains how recommendation algorithms shape visibility and checks claims against documented platform behaviour or studies.
Analyses a video game's rules, narrative and interactivity and checks claims against gameplay evidence.
Analyses release strategy and grosses for a film and checks figures against a named reporting source.
Breaks a screenplay into scenes, locations, cast and props for scheduling and checks the breakdown against the script pages.
Plans an edit with assembly, rough cut and sound passes and checks continuity across the cut list.
mcp: Enhance responses with scholarly research and citations
